plan.title: The Sigmoid Curve
plan.story: When modeling growth or decision thresholds, a simple linear scale often fails because real-world systems saturate at extremes. We need a function that maps any input smoothly between zero and one. The logistic sigmoid function provides this smooth transition, taking an input value and compressing it into a bounded range. By adjusting the steepness parameter, we can control how abruptly the transition occurs around the midpoint.
plan.cardDescription: Explore how the logistic sigmoid curve maps continuous inputs between zero and one. Adjust the steepness parameter to see how it changes the transition around the midpoint.
plan.learningGoal: Explain why changing steepness preserves the sigmoid bounds.
plan.instructions: Adjust the steepness slider to change how fast the curve transitions from zero to one. Observe the marker output update in real time.

scene.description: One curve, a fixed-input marker, a plain-word callout, an output readout and one steepness slider.

entities.label: Sigmoid curve
entities.purpose: Show output as a function of input.

entities.label: Selected point
entities.purpose: Link an input coordinate to its output.

quantities.label: Steepness k
quantities.reference: At x0 the slope is k / 4.

quantities.label: Midpoint x₀
quantities.meaning: Input at the centre of the transition.
quantities.reference: The output at x0 is one half. Increasing x0 shifts the curve right.

quantities.label: Marker x
quantities.meaning: Input coordinate of the selected point on the curve.
quantities.reference: The marker readout is y evaluated at this input.

quantities.label: Output y
quantities.meaning: Dimensionless output at x; strictly between zero and one for finite inputs. Positive is upward.

quantities.label: Slope dy/dx
quantities.meaning: Signed derivative of y with respect to x. Positive means the curve rises to the right.
quantities.reference: slope = k / (2 + exp(k * (x - x0)) + exp(-k * (x - x0)))

quantities.label: Output y
quantities.meaning: Dimensionless output at the selected input xMarker; the same curve, not a second rule.

observations.text: The output approaches either bound without reaching it at a finite input.

checkpoints.label: Default curve
checkpoints.expected: The marker lies on the curve and its readout is the output at the marked input.

checkpoints.label: Least steep
checkpoints.expected: The transition is gentler; its output stays within the same bounds.

checkpoints.label: Most steep
checkpoints.expected: The transition is sharper around its midpoint; its output stays within the same bounds.

mode.initialState: The curve at the default parameters with its linked marker; no elapsed time.

controls.label: Steepness k
controls.selectionReason: A continuous slider exposes nearby values and intermediate changes in the curve.

controls.label: Reset experiment
controls.purpose: Restore the default parameters and marker.
controls.selectionReason: One reset restores all linked settings together.
controls.effect: Restores the default parameters and marker input.

assumptions: Dimensionless logistic with positive steepness; a finite displayed input domain.
limitations: The plot shows a finite input interval; its bounds describe the full logistic.

claims.text: The output is strictly between zero and one for finite inputs with positive steepness.
claims.check: exp(z) > 0, hence 1 + exp(z) > 1 and its reciprocal is strictly between zero and one.
